lines.text: Some Muisca figures that look golden are about two thirds copper.
lines.say: Some MWEES-kah figures that look golden are about two thirds copper.

lines.text: Smiths heated the piece until its surface copper turned to oxide.
An acid from plants then washed the oxide away.
That left a skin rich in gold, which was then polished.
That skin is only a few thousandths of a millimeter thick.
The wax for the models came from stingless bees.
Some Zenu ornaments that look like twisted wire were cast whole.

post.caption: Tumbaga is copper dressed as gold. Some Muisca figures that look golden are about two thirds copper. Smiths heated the piece until its surface copper turned to oxide. An acid from plants then washed the oxide away. That left a skin rich in gold, which was then polished. That skin is only a few thousandths of a millimeter thick. The wax for the models came from stingless bees. Some Zenu ornaments that look like twisted wire were cast whole. The word tumbaga traces back to an Asian word for copper. The Muisca raft in the Gold Museum was cast in one pour.
